candidates.label: Acute inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to thrombotic occlusion of saphenous vein graft
missing_or_uncertain: Troponin negative at 2 hours may be early; ECG changes in paced rhythm may be non-diagnostic

candidates.label: Acute inferoposterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to graft occlusion
missing_or_uncertain: Posterior involvement not confirmed; ST depression in V2/V3 may be reciprocal to inferior injury

candidates.label: Acute non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) due to graft occlusion
missing_or_uncertain: ST elevation may be discordant due to paced rhythm, not meeting STEMI criteria; troponin negative at 2 hours is early

candidates.label: Acute coronary syndrome due to acute occlusion of native obtuse marginal artery (graft occlusion as incidental finding)
missing_or_uncertain: Obtuse marginal lesions may be chronic; acute graft thrombosis is more likely culprit

candidates.label: Acute myocardial infarction in the setting of paced rhythm with ECG changes of uncertain significance
missing_or_uncertain: ECG interpretation limited by biventricular pacing; resolution after catheterization supports ischemia

response.rationale: The acute presentation with chest pain, new inferior ST elevation, and confirmed thrombotic graft occlusion strongly supports acute inferior STEMI due to graft thrombosis. The early negative troponin does not exclude MI given the 2-hour window. The ST depression in V2/V3 is likely reciprocal to inferior injury rather than posterior, making D2 less likely. NSTEMI is less likely because ST elevation is present, though paced rhythm may confound. Native vessel disease is chronic and not the acute culprit. The overall picture is most consistent with D1.
